claims.text: House soba is nihachi (buckwheat + wheat), kneaded and cut in-shop, so wheat flour is present throughout soba preparation and surfaces.
Soba is served in a dashi-based tsuyu; typical Japanese soba tsuyu and soy sauce contain wheat. No wheat-free seasoning is documented.
Broth is a bonito-and-kombu dashi (contains fish), and onigiri fillings include salmon and Noto pork; tempura is fried in a shared setting.

name: のど黒めし本舗 いたる (Nodoguro-meshi Honpo Itaru)

claims.text: Dishes are seasoned-rice fish bowls finished with condiments and a fish-bone dashi broth; these preparations conventionally use wheat-containing soy sauce and dashi seasonings, so the menu is not safe for strict gluten avoidance.
Entirely seafood-based (nodoguro, yellowtail, Kaga fish) with fish-bone broth; no vegan options are documented.

name: 能加万菜 市場屋 近江町総本店 (Noukabanzai Ichibaya Omicho Sohonten)

claims.text: Sushi and seafood bowls are served with standard wheat-based soy sauce, and local ishiru (fermented-fish) seasoning and dashi are used throughout the menu.
The menu is built entirely around fresh fish and shellfish from Omicho Market, including raw seafood bowls, nigiri sushi, crab dishes and fish-based Kanazawa oden; no vegan items are documented.
An English menu is available, which can help travelers identify ingredients.

name: おでん ゑびす (Oden Ebisu)

claims.text: Menu is oden, sashimi, and obanzai cooked in a shared bonito-kombu dashi with wheat-based soy sauce and served in a tiny counter kitchen; cross-contamination risk is high and no gluten-free handling is documented.
Kanazawa oden and obanzai are conventionally seasoned with wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.
Core broth is bonito (fish) dashi and the menu features sashimi, shellfish, and char siu, so even vegetable items are simmered in animal-based stock.

name: おでん居酒屋 三幸 本店 (Oden Izakaya Miyuki Honten)

claims.text: Oden is simmered communally in one shared dashi pot containing wheat-gluten fu (車麩) and soy-sauce-based broth, so all oden items share gluten-contaminated liquid.
As a Kanazawa oden house, the simmering broth is built on dashi seasoned with soy sauce (standard wheat-containing shoyu); no gluten-free tamari is mentioned.
The base dashi is made from chicken bones, bonito and dried sardines, and the oden pot simmers fishcakes and whelk, so even vegetable items absorb animal-based broth.
All ingredients share one communal oden pot built on a wheat-soy and bonito broth, so cross-contact is unavoidable for gluten-free or vegan diners.
The signature dashi is made with dark soy sauce (koikuchi), which contains wheat, simmered with bonito.
The broth is simmered with meat (beef tendon) and seafood; vegetable items such as daikon and Kaga vegetables are cooked in the same animal-based pot.
All oden, including otherwise plant-based items like daikon and tofu, is simmered together in a shared fish-and-soy dashi, so cross-contact with wheat and fish is unavoidable.
The broth and seasoning are traditional Japanese soy- and miso-based, which means wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free alternative is documented.
The base dashi is made from dried sardines (niboshi), and every item shares that fish broth, so no dish is free of animal products.

name: おでん よし坊 (Oden Yoshibou)

claims.text: Oden is cooked communally in a single soy-sauce-and-dashi pot containing wheat-based items such as fish cakes, chikuwa and fried tofu, so heavy cross-contact with gluten is inherent to the dish.
The broth is a soy-sauce-based dashi; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so the broth and most simmered items are not gluten-free.
The shared simmering broth is a fish/seafood dashi and includes seafood such as whole bai-gai (whelk), so vegan separation is not possible.
Cooking avoids chemical seasonings, with broth salinity measured daily and seasoning adjusted to the day's conditions for a gentle, ingredient-forward taste.
